comparisons.D32: Use L with d_n rows and m columns and covariance L L-transpose + I_d, centered multivariateGaussian, and Measure.pi over n observations. The matrix needs a proof of the intended PSD/positive-definite covariance to avoid the constructor’s non-PSD Dirac fallback. Keep the factor dimension m as the loading column count, without inferring full column rank or row sparsity from this sampling-law definition. The product lives on finite coordinate tuples, not an algebraic tensor product.

rows.result: Function.support is generated additively from mulSupport and is exactly the set of inputs at which a function is not zero; choosing the codomain to be a row vector gives row support.
rows.gap: Identify the source’s positive row nonzero-count condition with nonzero rows and transport its one-based indices.

comparisons.D33: Treat the matrix as the function j ↦ L_j,: with values in m-dimensional vectors. Function.support then selects j with a nonzero entire row, equivalent to positive l0 count for a finite row. This is row support rather than the support of the flattened entry function or topological support of a measure. A short equivalence proof and the [d_n]-to-Fin d_n index map remain.

rows.result: Function.support supplies the row-index set and Set.powerset supplies all support subsets. These are sufficient predicates for exact-support cells, but do not package variable matrix shapes or their disjoint union.
rows.gap: Define tagged loading spaces with exact row support and prove their disjointness and finite model-count formula.

comparisons.D34: The cell is {L : Matrix (Fin d_n) (Fin m) Real | Function.support L = S}, with S a subset of row indices, preserving equality rather than containment. For each fixed m distinct supports are disjoint; across different m use dependent tagged matrix spaces to represent the claimed disjointness. Set.powerset on the finite row universe represents all supports; m_max times 2^d_n needs a cardinality proof. This does not restrict every model to at most s_n rows.

rows.gap: Assemble the row spike-and-slab prior and its dimension-dependent weights, proving probability normalization on the tagged model space.

comparisons.D35: Equation (5.10) uses a point spike at the whole zero row, Gaussian slab with covariance tau_0 I_m (tau_0 is covariance scale, not a squared standard deviation), and weight omega=d_n^(-(1+a_0)m). Prove 0≤omega≤1 from the dimension and positive constant conditions, form each nonnegative weighted two-measure sum and then the product over d_n rows. The model weights 1/|M_n| require a nonempty finite model set. Embed varying m into the hierarchical parameter space; the APIs do not establish the sparsity regularization or posterior contraction claims.

comparisons.D36: For each row choose psi_j in R^m, Phi_j positive definite and nu_j in [0,1], form (1-nu_j) delta_0 + nu_j N(psi_j,Phi_j) and product across rows. Positive definiteness must be proved for each covariance; do not specialize Phi_j to diagonal matrices or infer independence within a row. Values nu_j=0 or 1 are allowed. This builds a family of distributions, not a variational optimizer, and does not enforce one fixed exact support S because support cells have been merged.

comparisons.D30: Equation (4.5) is the finite product of g_N(0,1)(Y_i-f(x_i)); equivalently each response has Gaussian mean f(x_i), variance one. Inputs are fixed in [0,1]^d, so no input sampling law belongs in this product. The scalar density and law use a variance argument, here exactly 1. The finite product construction needs a joint density identification; the prose about possible unknown-variance extension does not change the theorem’s unit-variance model.

rows.result: The inspected theorem identifies finite Euclidean norm with the square root of the sum of squared coordinate norms. Evaluation at the fixed design points and a factor 1/sqrt(n) give the source expression for positive n.
rows.gap: Define the scaled finite-design evaluation seminorm and prove the empirical-distance formula with the source sample-size domain.

comparisons.D31: Use the Euclidean vector i ↦ f_0(x_i)-f_1(x_i) and divide its norm by sqrt(n); nonnegative square-root algebra gives the displayed root mean square when n>0. EuclideanSpace.norm_eq supplies the sum-of-squares identity, while the ordinary function-space Pi norm would be a sup norm. Distinct functions can agree at all observed points, so the result is a pseudometric on functions rather than a separating metric or population L2 distance. Preserve repeated design indices.

comparisons.D28: For B_n>0, cond volume (Ioo (-B_n) B_n) has finite positive interval mass, and its J_(K,M)-fold finite product represents Pi_n,(K,M); endpoint inclusion is Lebesgue-null. Mix the embedded model laws with exp(-a_0(KM)^2 log n) divided by the entire architecture sum. Retain a_0>0, dependence on n and architecture and independence from the truth. A nonempty finite set suffices for normalization; where a countable set is intended one must prove finite positive total weight rather than use nonsummable real tsum=0.
